label: verify-t6-flyingfish-data

claims.claim: Deng 2019 3-DOF runs all launch at fixed 20 m/s; 45.4 m (alpha0=0, gamma=25) and 13.2 m apex (alpha0=10, gamma=40) come from different runs.
claims.source_says: The take-off speed is fixed at 20 m s-1 for all the calculations... for 0 = 0, a maximum distance of 45.4 m is achieved at = 25... for 0 = 10... a maximum height of 13.2 m is reached at = 40.
claims.note: Downloaded the Zenodo PDF; section 3.3 matches exactly, including the 41.5 m / 3.47 s range peak of the alpha0=10 run.

claims.claim: Makiguchi 2013 gives leap speeds 3.87-5.15 m/s but no per-leap airborne time, so prediction P3 cannot be tested.
claims.source_says: the flying fish were estimated to leap from the water surface at speeds of 3.9 to 5.2 m s-1 ... predicted to reach 3.87 to 5.15 m s-1 when jumping from
claims.note: Speeds match; text search finds only acceleration duration and no airborne or flight time per leap (absence from my text search, not a full read).

claims.claim: Park and Choi arithmetic reproduces (L/Dmax 4.37, CLmax 0.78): ranges 22.3/50.1/89.1 m, vmin 9.85 m/s, with a 9.43-10.26 m/s rounding band.
claims.note: Table 2 row confirmed; repro.py reproduces 22.27/50.11/89.09 m, vmin 9.85 and the 9.43-10.26 band, and 4.37*v^2/2g gives 22.27 and 50.11 m for v=10 and 15 m/s.

claims.claim: Daane 2021 Data S1 reproduces: 49 flying fish with pectoral/SL 0.406-0.823; 14 with SL>=15 cm span 0.656-0.757; 3 above 0.76; 2 above 0.79.
claims.source_says: repro.py output: Daane-ff-min 0.406, Daane-ff-max 0.823, Daane-SL15-range 0.656-0.757, above-0.76: 3, above-0.79: 2
claims.note: Min, max, range and both counts reproduce from the cached xlsx via the agent's own script; I did not open the xlsx independently, the original paper's supplement, or confirm the 49 and 14 counts.

overall: All four key claims hold on what I checked. Claims 1 and 2 were checked against the original PDFs and match. Claim 3 reproduces from the cached Park and Choi table and arithmetic. Claim 4 is only partly independent. The Daane figures came from the agent's repro.py, which I re-ran, and I did not go back to the original supplement.
